text_blocks.snippet: Yes, COVID-19 infection during pregnancy can increase the risk of preterm birth. Studies have shown a link between COVID-19 and a higher rate of preterm births. For example, one study observed an increase in preterm births from 7.1% to 8.3% between July 2020 and February 2023, according to the National Institutes of Health (NIH). Another study noted a rise in preterm birth rates of 5.4% in 2020 and 2-4% in 2021.

text_blocks.snippet: While the exact reasons for this link are still being investigated, it's thought that COVID-19 infection can trigger inflammatory responses that may contribute to premature labor. The pandemic also led to changes in healthcare practices, which may have also played a role in the observed increase in preterm births.
